Critical t of the Waller-Duncan k-ratio test

Source: R/tests-extra.R
waller_critical.Rd

The Bayesian critical value t_B(K, F, q, f) of Waller and Duncan (1969), computed by numerical integration of the posterior expected losses (see waller_duncan()). Two means differ when their difference exceeds t_B * SE, the Bayes least significant difference. The value decreases as the observed F grows: with a small F the means are shrunk towards each other and few differences are declared.

Usage

waller_critical(K = 100, q, f, F)

Arguments

K

Ratio of the seriousness of a type I error to that of a type II error (50, 100 and 500 roughly match alpha = 0.10, 0.05 and 0.01).

q, f

Degrees of freedom of the treatments and of the error.

F

Observed F ratio of the treatments.

Value

A numeric vector of critical values (arguments are recycled).

References

Waller, R. A. and Duncan, D. B. (1969). A Bayes rule for the symmetric multiple comparisons problem. Journal of the American Statistical Association 64, 1484-1503.

Waller, R. A. and Kemp, K. E. (1975). Computations of Bayesian t-values for multiple comparisons. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation 4, 169-171.

Examples

waller_critical(100, q = 5, f = 24, F = 14.37)
#> [1] 1.918732
waller_critical(100, q = 4, f = 20, F = c(2, 5, 10, 100))
#> [1] 2.508500 2.143551 1.991624 1.873337
